about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Little new since midday: Texas yields were cut again in the November forecast, which supports the short-crop story, and Dec held its Friday gains near 78.7. The roughly 4¢ Dec/Mar carry still signals that certificated cotton is expected at delivery, so Dec longs face that overhang.
events: Texas cotton yield lowered again in November forecast (RFD-TV)
Cotton futures held onto Friday gains into the afternoon (Barchart)
Trade deals seen opening room for more US cotton exports (Brownfield)

sugar.fundamental: Nothing new out of Brazil this afternoon; Mar is holding about 18.40, above the 18.35–18.38 band, on short covering with crude. The weak real still favours mill hedging and sugar-heavy mixes, so the bounce is technical rather than a tighter Brazil balance.
events: Sugar holding key support after the real-driven drop (ADMIS)

coffee.fundamental: Arabica gave back its early gain as the real tumbled again, which loosens Brazil's farmer selling and export flow. The exchange side is unchanged: ICE certified stocks are still drawing, which keeps Dec firm relative to the Brazil-driven pressure on deferreds.
events: Coffee erased early gains as the Brazilian real fell (Barchart)
Dec back near 279 after probing 285.75 (desk quote)
Brazil coffee exports running well above last year (ADMIS, Barchart)

cocoa.fundamental: Afternoon flow adds to the weather story: heavy Ivory Coast rains are now hampering transport of beans to port, not just harvesting, which slows arrivals. Dec is up about 1% near 5,120; rising ICE stocks and industry surplus estimates still keep the near-term balance comfortable.
events: Heavy rains disrupt cocoa transport in Ivory Coast; prices climb (Barchart)
Ivorian weather agency warns El Niño could cut output ~25% (Reuters, ADMIS)
Dec cocoa ~5,120, up ~1% on the day (desk quote)
